title: Lemonaid vs FutureClinic: two ways to get everyday care online
summary: Lemonaid Health vs FutureClinic: compare Lemonaid's typical $25 condition consults and clinical team with FutureClinic's $40 one-to-one physician visits.
body_markdown:
## How do consultation prices and prescriptions compare?


As of October 2026, Lemonaid Health's[consultation fee page](https://lemonaidhealthcare.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/41864085576731-How-much-does-a-medical-consultation-with-a-healthcare-provider-cost) states "Our consultation fee is typically $25" for most visits, with medicine extra, and its[weight loss service](https://lemonaidhealthcare.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/41862915326107-How-much-does-the-Lemonaid-Health-Weight-Loss-service-cost) costs "$49 per month for ongoing treatment support" plus medicine. At FutureClinic, there is no subscription needed: you pay $40 to match with the best-fit doctor in the clinic, or pick a specific physician at their listed price, typically $20 to $100.


Because FutureClinic sells no drugs and physicians earn nothing extra for any prescription or test they order, the doctor you message has one incentive only: helping you, with zero reason to upsell a medication or lab panel. Your physician has no house formulary steering their choices, can write for whichever brand or generic fits your case, and never requires an active subscription just to keep refills going. When you take a stable maintenance drug and your physician judges a multi-month supply safe, one visit can cover several months at once if your doctor decides it's right for you. Prescriptions go to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, with a cash discount coupon. Both services let you use insurance at a local pharmacy, and FutureClinic helps with prior authorizations, offers discounted lab tests, and does not prescribe controlled medicines like stimulants, benzodiazepines, opioids, testosterone or phentermine.


For ongoing care, Lemonaid's[Primary Care Complete](https://www.lemonaidhealth.com/services/primary-care) membership starts at $99/month for individuals or $178/family as of October 2026 ("Cancel anytime in the first 30 days"), with "the personal attention of the same doctor" and a one-hour video visit. Its App Store seller as of October 2026 is SteadyMD, Inc., and 23andMe[sold Lemonaid Health in September 2025](https://hlth.com/insights/news/bambu-ventures-and-innova-acquire-23andme-s-lemonaid-health-for-10m-2025-09-19) for $10 million. On FutureClinic, you can stay with the same doctor[per visit](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) , or, if they offer one, join their optional membership, typically $25 to $100 a month (median $50), for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time.


## Which service fits your situation better?


Which fits you better: Lemonaid Health's condition-by-condition forms and membership terms, or one physician you can message whenever a health issue comes up?


Lemonaid Health is a strong option if you want a typical $25 consult for a menu condition, a membership from $99 a month that starts with a one-hour video visit, or care across all 50 states. FutureClinic is the stronger option if all you wanted was an expert physician (MD, DO or MBBS) one-to-one, who sends a Human Signature, treats other problems in their specialty, works from your one medical record alongside any other FutureClinic specialists you see, and comes with nothing attached.


## Messaging a physician for everyday primary care in 33 states and D.C.


FutureClinic works in 33 states and Washington, D.C.: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. Your doctor must be licensed in the state you're in; if you don't see your state, try anyway as new licenses are added.


Start at[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) , or from the AI app you already use, including[ChatGPT](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-real-doctor-to-chatgpt) ,[Claude](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-doctor-to-claude) , Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, Meta Muse and Instinct, at[futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) . To get started in an AI app that reads the web, send your AI:


` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.


> Use FutureClinic to find me a doctor in my state to review my blood pressure and thyroid labs.


See our[editorial standards](https://futureclinic.com/blog/editorial-standards) . FutureClinic is not for emergencies: call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
